sections.churn_summary: Hold-buffer guards are aligned on every active book (`exit_confirm_screens=2`, `reentry_cooldown_screens=1`, `min_rebalance_notional_gbp=10.0`), and the latest pass shows no guard activation: `buffered_holdings=0`, empty `exit_streak` and `reentry_cooldown` everywhere, `duplicate_day_skip=false`, and `adjacent_flip_count=0` with empty `adjacent_side_flips` in the 7-day window. Recent activity is mixed—primary `ai_judgment_fair` is quieter at 4 trades in 7d (2 buys, 1 sell, 1 trim) with `last_run.trade_count=2`, while control `buy_tier_level` logged 18 trades in 7d (12 sells / 12 full exits) but `last_run.trade_count=0`—yet lifetime primary drag remains elevated (`cost_drag=0.1386`, watch alert) compared with epoch-scoped drag on the same book (`learning_track_epoch_datum.cost_drag` implied via epoch `total_costs`/`epoch_nav`: epoch `cost_drag=0.0198`, `post_apply_trade_count=28`). The 7-day buffered-hold replay for `ai_judgment_fair` and `buy_tier_level` still does not separate `exit_confirm_screens=1` vs `2` (`trade_count_delta_lower_minus_higher=0`, `cost_drag_delta_lower_minus_higher=0.0` on both). The single biggest operational learning gap is that post-exit evidence is still empty on active books (`exit_shadow` for `ai_judgment_fair` and `buy_tier_level`: `closed_count=0` despite `open_count=14` and `29` respectively), so guard tuning cannot be validated against realized exit paths while the 7-day screen replay stays tied.
